title: The Old Man Made Young variant

keywords: the old man made young variant
full_text:
A holy wanderer traveling the countryside visited a blacksmith's forge. Seeing the smith's aged father trembling with palsy, bent double with years, the wanderer took pity on the old man. He placed him gently into the roaring furnace coals, blew the bellows with rhythmic grace, and quenched him in a vat of pure spring water.

To the smith's astonishment, the ancient father emerged as a vigorous, handsome youth of twenty, glowing with health and vitality!

When the wanderer departed, the proud blacksmith thought to himself: "What a marvelous art! Why should I hammer horseshoes when I can make old folks young and charge a mountain of gold?"

He persuaded his frail, eighty-year-old mother-in-law to climb into the forge. The blacksmith piled on coal, pumped the bellows with frantic speed, and heated the furnace to white heat. The poor woman shrieked in agony, while the foolish smith blew harder, convinced the magic was taking effect.

When he hauled her out and plunged her into the water barrel, she lay scorched and blackened, barely clinging to life.

Just then, the holy wanderer returned, heard the lamentations, and miraculously restored the scorched woman to health. He sternly rebuked the arrogant blacksmith: "Do not meddle with mysteries beyond your understanding; stick to your anvil and let divine grace tend to mortal life!"
moral: Miraculous healing belongs to divine grace; foolish presumption leads to disaster.
